Issued at 225 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

Today-Tonight...Quasi-zonal flow in the mid-levels remains 
positioned across the Florida peninsula today, supporting 
localized high pressure at the surface along with mostly dry 
conditions. Northwesterly winds are forecast locally, remaining 
around 10 mph. A slow moistening of the atmosphere is anticipated
through today as PWATs increase to 1.1-1.3", manifesting 
primarily as increasing cloud coverage across east central 
Florida. There is a low chance for some passing light showers 
tonight, but confidence remains too low to include within the 
forecast. Temperatures are forecast to be seasonable areawide, 
with highs in the 70s and lows in the upper 50s to mid 60s. At the
beaches, there is a moderate risk of rip currents today. Always 
swim near a lifeguard and follow the advice of local beach safety 
officials.

Tuesday-Thursday...A strong mid-level trough across the central 
US becomes further enhanced by a cut-off low digging southward 
from Canada and across the midwest on Wednesday, with gradual 
progression towards the southeastern US Wednesday night into 
Thursday. The mid-level trough axis will be directly over the 
Florida peninsula on Thursday, lifting northeastward through 
Thursday afternoon. At the surface, a weakening frontal boundary 
drifting across the southeastern US will stall across north 
Florida and the Gulf on Tuesday. As the boundary slowly meanders 
southward, an area of low pressure is forecast to develop across 
the southeastern Gulf and along the stalled boundary Tuesday night
into Wednesday. As mid level support arrives Wednesday into 
Thursday, the low will lift northeastward across the south Florida
peninsula, shifting away from Florida by Thursday night. Overall,
this evolving pattern is anticipated to result in a surge of 
moisture locally starting on Tuesday, resulting in increasing rain
and storm chances through mid-week. 

Rain chances on Tuesday will be focused across the local Atlantic
waters but will expand Tuesday night towards the peninsula as the
low develops and onshore flow advects moisture westward(PoPs 
30-60%). As the low begins lifting across south Florida, rain 
chances increase to 60-80% on Wednesday, falling to 30-50% into 
the overnight hours as the low begins to pull away from the area. 
There is also a 20% chance of storm development embedded within 
activity Wednesday into Wednesday night, with chances diminishing 
into Thursday morning. While the surface low is anticipated to be 
farther north by Thursday, the mid-level trough axis directly 
overhead will support additional scattered showers across east 
central Florida behind the low, especially for northern portions 
of the forecast area. Deviated from the NBM to show this, with a 
20-30% chance of showers added to the forecast. As stated with 
prior forecasts, discrepancies in timing between global models and
ensembles continue, but there is increasing confidence that 
Wednesday will be the wettest day across east central Florida of 
the three days. Initial rainfall totals look to be between 0.5-1" 
across the interior west of I-95 and along the coast from Cape 
Canaveral northward. Along the southern Brevard coast and the 
Treasure Coast, rainfall totals of 1-2" are forecast. There is a 
20-40% chance for places from the Cape southward to see rainfall 
totals greater than 2", but there remains some uncertainty given 
the discrepancies between guidance. Changes in projected rainfall 
totals will be possible as the evolution and track of the low 
become clearer in the coming days. Regardless of totals, however, 
any rainfall across fully saturated portions of east central 
Florida will likely result in additional or worsening flooding, 
with the greatest concern primarily focused across coastal 
communities and those along the St. Johns River.

The passing disturbance will result in rapidly building seas and 
the return of poor to hazardous beach conditions through the 
middle of this week. Additionally, high astronomical tides are 
forecast to return along the east central Florida coast, enhancing
the potential for minor coastal flooding. Rough surf and minor 
coastal flooding will increase the risk of minor beach erosion, 
and a high risk of rip currents is anticipated along the entire
coast. Seas will be slow to subside beyond Thursday.

Friday-Sunday...High pressure builds across the Gulf and the 
southeastern US into Friday behind the low, resulting in drier air
and lower rain chances (below 20%) Friday and most of Saturday.
